title: Composition and inverse transformations
section: Linear Transformations ▷ A Note on Inverses and Compositions
terms: composition of linear maps; inverse linear transformation; matrix order in composition.

exposition.text:
The composition T ◦ S applies S first and T second. If their matrices are B and A with com-
patible intermediate bases, the composition matrix is AB. Composition remains linear and is
associative, but reversing the order generally changes the map or may make it undefined.
A bijective linear map has a linear inverse; the inverse matrix is the matrix inverse. For in-

question.text:
2 −1
On R define S(x, y) = (x + y, y) and T(x, y) = (x, y − x). What is (T ◦ S) (a, b)?
(A) (a − b, b) (B) (−b, a + b) (C) (b, a − b) (D) (a, b − a) (E) (a + b, a)

solution.text:
T (S(x, y)) = (x + y, −x). Solving a = x + y, b = −x gives x = −b, y = a + b, so the inverse
is (−b, a + b).

Linear maps S : R → R and T : R → R satisfy T ◦ S = I 2. What is dim ker T ?
R
(A) 0 (B) 1 (C) 2 (D) 3 (E) Cannot be determined

solution.text:
2
The identity factorization implies T is onto R , so its rank is 2. Its domain has dimension
3, and rank-nullity gives nullity 1.

The composition sends (x, y, z) to (x − z, 0). Its kernel is therefore the plane x = z,
parametrized as (s, t, s). A vector need only map under S into ker T ; it need not belong to
ker S.

every polynomial, hence the identity. Composition order matters even for two elementary
linear operators.
